title: 19. K8s Control Plane Internals, etcd & Upgrades
summary: Deep-dive mastery of Kubernetes control plane architecture, static pod manifests, etcd backup/restore, kubeadm multi-node upgrades, certificate rotation, and disaster recovery.
prerequisites: Linux systemd and journalctl daemon debugging
Kubernetes Core Architecture (API Server, Controller Manager, Scheduler, etcd)
PKI and TLS X.509 certificate validation
learningObjectives: Safely backup, snapshot, and restore the etcd key-value datastore without quorum loss
Inspect, modify, and troubleshoot kubelet static pod manifests in /etc/kubernetes/manifests
Execute zero-downtime control plane and worker node upgrades using kubeadm and drain policies
Check, rotate, and verify control plane TLS certificates with kubeadm certs

curriculumModules.title: etcd Architecture, Raft Consensus & Snapshot Restoration
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: etcd is the single source of truth in Kubernetes. Maintaining quorum (N/2 + 1) and executing periodic point-in-time snapshot saves to durable storage is essential for disaster recovery.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: External or stacked multi-master etcd cluster with automated daily snapshots and cross-region replication.

curriculumModules.title: Control Plane Lifecycle, kubeadm Upgrades & Certificate Rotation
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Kubernetes version upgrades require sequential minor version increments (e.g. 1.31 -> 1.32). Control plane components are cordoned, upgraded via kubeadm upgrade apply, and verified before workers.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Rolling canary node drain with PodDisruptionBudgets protecting stateful workloads during OS and kubelet upgrades.

labs.title: etcd Snapshot Backup and Point-in-Time Disaster Recovery
labs.scenario: You are the Lead Kubernetes Administrator. Before a major cluster schema migration, company policy requires taking an immutable etcd snapshot and verifying its cryptographic integrity.
labs.productionContext: In enterprise production, etcd snapshot saves must run on dedicated volumes and verify key revisions before schema changes.
objectives: Execute etcdctl snapshot save to persist cluster state to /var/lib/etcd/etcd-snapshot.db
Verify snapshot health using etcdctl endpoint health
Record backup metadata ConfigMap in the kube-system namespace
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: etcd-backup-audit
  namespace: kube-system
data:
  snapshotPath: "/var/lib/etcd/etcd-snapshot.db"
  status: "verified"

steps.title: Take etcd Database Snapshot
steps.instruction: Run etcdctl snapshot save to backup the key-value store to /var/lib/etcd/etcd-snapshot.db

steps.title: Verify etcd Cluster Endpoint Health
steps.instruction: Check the health of the etcd endpoint before proceeding.

steps.title: Deploy Backup Audit ConfigMap
steps.instruction: Apply the etcd-backup-audit ConfigMap to kube-system to record verification proof.

validationRules.description: etcdctl snapshot save command was successfully executed
validationRules.remediation: Execute 'etcdctl snapshot save /var/lib/etcd/etcd-snapshot.db' in the terminal.

validationRules.description: ConfigMap etcd-backup-audit exists in kube-system with status verified
validationRules.name: etcd-backup-audit
validationRules.remediation: Apply the starter manifest to create ConfigMap etcd-backup-audit in kube-system.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure you specify the full path /var/lib/etcd/etcd-snapshot.db when running etcdctl snapshot save.

labs.title: Node Maintenance, Cordon/Drain & kubeadm Upgrades
labs.scenario: A security advisory requires upgrading worker nodes to v1.32.0. Before performing the upgrade, safely cordon and drain worker-01 to evict non-DaemonSet workloads.
labs.productionContext: Node draining honors PodDisruptionBudgets (PDB) to prevent service degradation during OS patching and kubelet upgrades.
objectives: Cordon node kubelabs-worker-01 to mark it unschedulable
Drain node kubelabs-worker-01 to safely evict active pods
Plan control plane upgrade using kubeadm upgrade plan
Verify certificate expiration status using kubeadm certs check-expiration
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: upgrade-maintenance-audit
  namespace: default
data:
  targetVersion: "v1.32.0"
  nodeStatus: "drained"

steps.title: Cordon Worker Node
steps.instruction: Mark kubelabs-worker-01 as unschedulable to stop new pods from landing on it.

steps.title: Inspect Upgrade Plan and Certificates
steps.instruction: Run kubeadm upgrade plan and kubeadm certs check-expiration to verify readiness.

validationRules.name: kubelabs-worker-01
validationRules.remediation: Run 'kubectl cordon kubelabs-worker-01' to mark the node unschedulable.

validationRules.description: ConfigMap upgrade-maintenance-audit exists with nodeStatus drained
validationRules.name: upgrade-maintenance-audit
validationRules.remediation: Apply the starter manifest to record the upgrade audit.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Check 'kubectl get nodes' to verify kubelabs-worker-01 displays 'SchedulingDisabled'.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which etcd command creates a point-in-time backup of the datastore?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: etcdctl snapshot save <path> is the canonical CLI command to produce an immutable binary snapshot of etcd.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary difference between 'kubectl cordon' and 'kubectl drain'?
options: cordon deletes the node; drain restarts the kubelet
cordon marks a node unschedulable; drain marks it unschedulable AND evicts running non-DaemonSet pods
cordon is for worker nodes only; drain is for control-plane nodes only
cordon deletes namespaces; drain removes secrets
assessmentQuestions.explanation: cordon only marks the node unschedulable for future pods, whereas drain marks it unschedulable and actively evicts existing pods.
